title: Precision Hotswap Engine for runtime kernel dispatch across FP16/FP8/INT8
creator: Diego Rivera
description:
Problem: We need a low-latency, safe mechanism for switching kernel execution paths at runtime to use mixed-precision (FP16/FP8/INT8) variants without service disruption or accuracy regressions. Current dispatch is too coarse-grained (per-model) which forces entire requests on lower precision even when only a subset of layers are safe to quantize, or requires costly model duplication.

Goal: Build a 'Precision Hotswap Engine' (PHE) that can: (1) select per-layer execution kernels based on quantization profiles and live signal (latency headroom, memory pressure, accuracy confidence), (2) perform atomic switches of kernel variants mid-request when safe, (3) integrate with existing calibration workflows and accuracy validators, and (4) provide observability and rollback controls for canary rollouts.

Scope & deliverables:
- Runtime component that maintains a per-model precision plan and can atomically switch kernel pointers for individual layers or blocks.
- Compatibility matrix and verification step to ensure FP8/INT8 kernels preserve KV-cache layout and tensor layouts before swap.
- Integration with the calibration pipeline: download quant-profiles (FP8/INT8) produced by offline calibration CI and map them to runtime kernel candidates.
- Online accuracy validation harness: sampled requests re-run in parallel on a reference FP16 path to compute delta metrics (log-prob delta, token error rate) and drive confidence scoring.
- Canary rollout workflow in Console: route small % of traffic, live dashboards for p99/p50 latency and accuracy_regression_score, automatic fallback to FP16 if threshold breached.
- Unit and integration tests, and a stress test scenario that reproduces KV-cache pressure and memory fragmentation on multi-GPU nodes.

Non-goals: full model-recompilation in the path, user-facing API changes, hardware microcode changes.

Success metrics:
- No more than 2% median throughput regression relative to baseline FP16 for mixed workloads after enabling hotswap paths at 50% traffic.
- Accuracy regression < 0.5% measured by our evaluation harness on held-out prompt set.
- Rollback time under 5s for canary if accuracy or latency SLOs are violated.

Design notes:
1) Decision model: Precision Candidate Scorer that ranks kernels by a weighted sum of predicted accuracy hit (from calibration profile), measured latency delta (from benchmark table), and current runtime headroom. We will store precomputed per-layer cost/accuracy tuples in the model catalog metadata.
2) Atomic switch mechanism: maintain an indirection table of layer -> kernel function pointers plus a generation counter. Switch performed by publishing a new generation and flipping a pointer in a thread-safe manner; in-flight requests either drain or observe the new generation based on safe handoff rules.
3) KV-cache compatibility: All quantized kernels must guarantee identical KV-cache layout and type widening semantics when reading and writing cache entries. We will add a lightweight byte-level checksum stage after a switch on sampled requests to detect cache corruption early.
4) Calibration integration: calibration jobs in CI emit quant-profiles to s3://redwood-quant/profiles/{model}/{profile_id}. The runtime fetcher will validate profile signature, run a small compatibility smoke test (shape checks + forward consistency), and then enlist kernels as candidates.
5) Monitoring & gating: New console metrics: precision.swap.count, precision.swap.latency_ms, precision.rollback.count, precision.accuracy_delta. Alerts: accuracy_delta > 0.5% over 5m OR p99 latency increase >20% for canary group => automatic rollback.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- PHE can switch kernels for at least 6 open-source model architectures used in catalog without OOM or cache corruption.
- Canary flow successfully toggles 1% -> 10% -> 50% traffic for a calibration profile with no false-positives from the validation harness.
- Integration tests covering atomicity (in-flight requests handled), KV-cache checksum mismatch detection, and automatic rollback.
- Documentation for on-call teams and runbook for manual intervention published in Confluence.

Implementation plan (milestones):
A) API & indirection table (2w) - define kernel descriptor, generation counter, and safe flip semantics.
B) Compatibility validator + checksum (1w) - run byte-checks on sampled requests.
C) Calibration fetcher + profile mapping (1w) - integrate with S3 and model catalog.
D) Candidate scorer & policy engine (2w) - scoring, headroom signals, and gating.
E) Canary pipeline + Console integration (2w) - dashboards, alerts, rollout controls.
F) Tests & stress harness (2w) - multi-GPU reproduction, perf runs.

Rollout plan: internal dev cluster canary -> staged public canary in us-west-2 -> gradual scale with automatic guardrails.

Automatic rollback triggers and completes within 5s on threshold breach
Unit tests cover generation switch semantics and concurrent in-flight requests
comments: 2026-02-16 Priya Kapoor: Spun up initial indirection-table prototype. Verified pointer flip semantics on single-threaded runtime. Next: make thread-safe using atomic generation counters.

2026-02-20 Diego Rivera: Calibration CI wrote FP8 profiles to s3 for gpt-small and llama-7b. Initial compatibility check failed for llama-7b block-idx 3 due to layout mismatch; engineering to add a shim to normalize kv shapes.

2026-02-25 Priya Kapoor: Benchmarks on p4d.24xlarge show candidate INT8 kernel for gpt-small reduces token latency by ~14% but increases variance. Adding headroom-weighted policy to prefer FP8 on tail-sensitive routes.

2026-03-02 SRE (Maya Thompson): Ran stress harness; observed rare checksum mismatches under extreme memory fragmentation. Hypothesis: allocator alignment differs between kernels. Added alignment check and fixed allocator flags in PR #4289.

2026-03-07 Priya Kapoor: Deployed canary to internal dev cluster at 1% traffic using profile id profile-20260307-gpt-small-fp8. Eval harness reports accuracy_delta 0.12% at 5k sampled tokens. Proceeding to 10% tomorrow.
2026-03-10 Diego Rivera: PR 4278 merged with generation-counter atomicity fixes and initial console metrics. Created follow-up ENG-85012 for extended A/B evaluation across noisy prompt sets.
